newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Samancor to put bln rand into partnerships.
newsitem.headline: Samancor to put bln rand into partnerships.

text.p: South African ferrochrome giant Samancor Ltd aims to spend around a billion rand over the next two years on international joint ventures, financial director Chris Norval told Reuters on Thursday.
Samancor, with its core business in chrome and manganese, this year entered into three major joint ventures with Japanese and South Korean steel companies.
"We have done various joint ventures with offshore parties whereby we increased the utilisation and stablity of our operations," Norval said.
"The result of these joint ventures is that we will be, in the next two years, spending in excess of 500 million rand per annum on capital to bring those joint ventures to fruition."
In June the Advalloy joint venture was set up between Samancor, Japan Metals and Chemicals Co Ltd and Mitsui and Company Ltd.
The 200-million rand deal would see the annual production of 75,000 tonnes of refined manganese alloys.

In another deal in July, Samancor joined with Nisshin Steel and Nissho Iwai Corp to establish a joint venture in South Africa to ensure a stable long-term supply of ferrochrome for the Japanese companies.
Samancor also cemented its existing relationship with South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co Ltd (Posco) by establishing a joint venture with Posco subsidiary, Postrade Inc and Samsun Corp.
Under the agreement, Samancor will supply Posco with 50,000 tonnes of ferrochrome a year.
Samancor lifted its attributable income for the year ended June 30 by 82 percent to 676 million rand.
But Norval said on Thursday that the company was not confident of repeating the performance.
"We had a very good year but the markets are weakening and we are probably going to have a worse year in the coming one."

The company was expecting profits in its chrome division to drop due to lower prices while start-up costs at the Columbus Stainless joint venture -- a joint venture with Highveld Steel and Vanadium Corp and the state's Industrial Development Corporation -- continued to weigh on Samancor.

Norval said options under evaluation for Columbus -- one of the largest stainless steel facilities in the world -- included the addition of further cold rolling capacity and possible cold rolling ventures located offshore nearer to end markets.

"The timing of that will be determined by the start-up profile and the opportunities that present themselves. You either will do it at (Columbus) or offshore, and that will be a trade off between your capital expenditure and access to markets," Norval added.
Samancor said in its annual report that it was considering disposing or diluting its non-core assets to enhance its balance sheet.
"It is a strategy which will happen if we find something like the Quarzwerke deal. If we don't find something sensible like that then it won't happen," Norval said.
Samancor plans to dispose of 60 percent of its Delmas Silica to Quarzwerke BV. Norval said the deal was still under discussion.
